subject.title: Add multi-gateway cron job coordination for HA deployments

question: Should distributed cron ownership be a core cron feature, a plugin-provided coordination API, or a requirement folded into the broader horizontal-scaling/runtime architecture work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend boundary, config shape, failure semantics, health/CLI surface, dependency posture, and relationship to broader HA architecture require maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design backend-neutral cron ownership
options.body: Define a generic cron lease or leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, SQLite, or plugin-backed deployments do not become competing one-off paths.

options.title: Fold into broader HA architecture
options.body: Make this issue a cron-specific requirement of the horizontal-scaling or distributed-runtime design and close it only after that design explicitly owns cron scheduling.

options.title: Document external-only operation
options.body: Keep built-in cron single-Gateway for now and document external scheduler or external lock patterns as the supported HA path.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral cron ownership
recommendation.body: Define a generic cron lease or leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, SQLite, or plugin-backed deployments do not become competing one-off paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest inspected cron scheduler history and already participated in the architecture-review discussion for this issue.
